explanation: Retrospective, context-free piece detector: at layer 0 the pole reads only the current token's embedding (GPT-NeoX uses RoPE, so there is no learned position vector), so its strength is a fixed lookup on the piece, not on its context - integrated gradients put 100% of the attribution on the peak token and 0% on anything before it, token identity explains 100% of the scan's variance, and every piece with a positive value reproduces that value exactly in running text (max deviation 1e-7 over a 140-token passage; the only larger differences are negative values clamped to zero by the pole), so ' terms' reads 1.046, the scan's own scale, in all sixteen of the scan's 'terms' snippets and at all six 'terms' positions of that test passage, whatever precedes or follows. Its input row is closest to the piece ' terms', and the pole fires on a graded, fixed halo of specialised non-core-English content pieces rather than on a concept: the text-unit lexeme is the core (' terms' 1.05, ' term' 0.79, 'Term' 0.66, bare 'terms' 0.59, capitalised ' Terms' only 0.24) together with pieces naming units of written text ('word'/'words' 0.77/0.66, 'sentences' 0.68, 'articles' 0.57, 'phrases' 0.50, 'paragraph' 0.44, 'folder' 0.45, 'documents' 0.41, 'alphabet' 0.36, 'vocabulary' 0.35, 'clause' 0.29), around them a halo of names ('Paris' 0.95, 'Haiti' 0.95, 'Brazil' 0.88, 'Wien' 0.78, 'Wilhelm' 0.75, 'Hilbert' 0.58), non-English function words (' des' 0.78, ' τις' 0.72, ' zum' 0.63) and programming/format identifiers (' FILE' 0.85, 'Window' 0.76, ' DWORD' 0.64, ' iterator' 0.62, ' errno' 0.60), while common English function words (' the' -0.05, ' and' -0.04, ' to' -0.03, ' of' 0.02), generic everyday nouns (' house' 0.12, ' water' -0.07, ' people' -0.12, ' money' -0.14) and digits stay silent; the halo is not semantic (' Paris' fires but ' London' 0.03, ' Rome' 0.18, ' Madrid' 0.02, ' Tokyo' -0.13 do not, and ' definition' 0.23, ' terminology' 0.15, ' title' -0.11 stay under the line), so a text is predicted active exactly when it contains a piece whose fixed value is at or above the protocol's 0.25-of-max line (5.1% of the vocabulary, about 2,550 pieces, most of them too rare to enter a 200k-token scan's trigger-token list), and its peak is simply the largest fixed value among those pieces. Nothing about the upcoming token is prepared: zero-ablating the pole moves the next-token distribution at the 'terms' position by KL ~1e-8, and the output side has no coherent promoted set (logit-lens kurtosis 3.2), consistent with an early-layer token key whose effect is carried by later layers.
